It is not a closing order (the type label closing_mourning is wrong; the WPA 1944 list, 1935 CSR 28, and the APP title agree): under the Civil Service Act of January 16, 1883 it amends paragraph 6 of subdivision VII of schedule A of the civil-service rules 'to read as follows': '6. Temporary clerks, carriers, and laborers required for part-time or intermittent work in the Postal Service in connection with the present holiday or seasonal business from this date to February 1, 1935.' Decision on its own terms. The order's one command is the rewrite of paragraph 6; under the strike-and-insert ruling the rewritten paragraph is the operative clause and continues, amended, until something ends it. Two candidate ends exist in held evidence. (a) The inserted text's own period: the paragraph excepts positions only 'from this date to February 1, 1935'. That period is part of the exception's definition, so after February 1, 1935 the paragraph excepted no position; the text itself is the evidence that its operation ended, and nothing held extended it (the WPA 1944 list shows no amendment of subdivision VII paragraph 6 between October 16, 1934 and October 19, 1935). (b) EO 7209 (October 19, 1935; held government-printed text, added here as SUPPLEMENT:EO7209) amends paragraph 6 'to read as follows' with a new period to February 1, 1936; its words show it replaced the paragraph's text, but by then the 1934 exception had already stopped operating. Under the evidence-decides ruling EO 7209 is not a default end, and here the earlier own-terms end is evidenced. Savings: appointments made under the exception during its period are accrued; they do not keep the exception operative. Earlier versions of paragraph 6 (EO 5731, 1931; EO 5930, 1932; EO 6352, 1933) precede this order and do not affect its end.

EO 7208 (October 19, 1935), read in full in the held American Presidency Project transcription (two held copies of the same page, sha256 shared), exempts George G. Identity: number, date, person and title agree across the APP page, the census register and the WPA 1944 numbered list. The order recites EO 6338 (October 14, 1933) and EO 6862 (September 30, 1934), recited earlier exemptions. Later orders further exempting the same person are held and added to this packet as source-supplement excerpts: EO 7475 (October 19, 1936) recites EO 6338, 6862 and 7208 and further exempts Hedgcock until July 1, 1937; EO 7645 (June 24, 1937) recites EO 6338, 6862, 7208 and 7475 ("periods totaling three years and eight months") and further exempts him until January 1, 1938. None says that the earlier order 'is amended' or alters its date; each recites the earlier exemption as a past grant ('who was exempted ... by Executive Order No. ...') and grants a further exemption 'until' a new date.
